newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods flatten on ample supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods flatten on ample supplies.

text.p: Ample supplies and light preweekend discussion froze U.S. West Coast products prices late, with flatness expected next week as a key refinery buyer stepped out of the market during maintenance work.
West Coast pricing was reacting to a 636,000 barrels build in gasoline stocks that left total inventories 2.4 million barrels above year-ago levels.
"Generally, the market is pretty well supplied," one West Coast trader.
On Friday, jet fuel reversed Thursday's slide and rose 3.00 cents to 67.50/68.50 cents a gallon.
The rebound came after yesterday's 4.50-cent price collapse in the wake of two large cargoes into Los Angeles.
"I would expect to see jet spring back," one trader said.
Chevron Corp said Friday they shut on Thursday a 60,000 barrel-per-day fluid catalytic cracker at its El Segundo refinery for several weeks of maintenance.
Los Angeles conventional regular gasoline stayed 62.50/63.50 cents a gallon, with San Francisco grades at their normal discount of 1.50 cents.
CARB-grade gasoline was unchanged this afternoon at 67/68.50 cents, making up some ground from yesterday's two cent loss.
Low sulphur diesel, usually three to four cents cheaper than jet, was talked 3.50 cents higher at 71/72 cents.
